problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y={x}^{2}-3x$ at the point $(-2,10).$
worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{2}-3x.$ Computing the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-3x)=2x-3.\end{aligned}
$$

We then compute ${f}^{′}(-2)$, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(-2)=2(-2)-3=-7.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we use the point-slope form with $m=-7$ and the coordinates of our point $(-2,10),$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(10) & =-7(x-(-2)) \\ y-10 & =-7(x+2) \\ y & =-7x-14+10 \\ y & =-7x-4.\end{aligned}
$$
